title: Exposure Corridor Scheduler — compact timeline and quick-snapshot rollback flow
creator: Marta Reyes
description: Design and prototype a compact ‘Exposure Corridor Scheduler’ for the Redwood Console rollouts surface. This ticket explores a condensed, single-line timeline for canary/A-B rollouts that surfaces: 1) per-slice traffic percent and audience, 2) realtime cost delta estimates per step, 3) quick-snapshot savepoints (immutable snapshots that enable sub-60s rollback to a prior snapshot), and 4) a prescriptive pause/inspect action that gates progression based on selected telemetry checks. The goal is to enable PMs and engineers to author progressive exposures faster while keeping rollback and cost implications explicit in the UI. This designs needs to be visually compact to live in the overview panel but expandable to a detail canvas for advanced edits.
acceptance_criteria: Compact timeline widget renders within the rollout list card without horizontal overflow
Users can create and name a snapshot at any step (snapshot persists to the rollout and is visible in the audit trail)
Progression action supports manual, timer-based, and signal-gated pauses
Cost delta estimate updates immediately when adjusting a step's traffic percentage
Rollback to snapshot completes visual flow simulation and produces a one-click revert action in the UI
ux_notes: Use condensed glyphs for pause/play/fast-back; expand to full labels on hover or on narrow-screen tap
Microcopy for snapshots: 'Snapshot created — captures model version, routing policy, and sampling config.'
Keyboard accessibility: timeline should be navigable with arrow keys and activation via Enter/Space
Animation: a 150ms ease-in between steps when simulating traffic shift to keep motion subtle but informative
Color semantics: green for safe/healthy, amber for warning-signal gates, red for failed checkpoints; also include patterned fill for colorblind accessibility
rollout_playback_steps: 1. Author: add steps and specify audience segment + percent (visual slider with numeric input)
2. Snapshot: click camera icon to create immutable snapshot — recorded in audit log with timestamp and optional note
3. Simulate: 'Preview Run' toggles simulation overlay showing expected latency and cost delta (based on recent 24h metrics)
4. Start: choose 'Manual' | 'Timer (minutes)' | 'Signal-gated' — signal selection lists preconfigured checks (error rate, p95 latency, hallucination score)
5. Pause: automatic pause on signal violation surfaces 'Inspect' (drill to traces, sample prompts, quality diff) or 'Force Continue' (with justification modal)
6. Rollback: from any paused/healthy state click snapshot -> 'Revert to snapshot' to open confirmation flow with estimated customer impact and token-cost delta
decision_log: Prefer immutable snapshots over step-level undo to simplify backend complexity and ensure auditability — discussed with Backend (ENG) on 2026-03-03
Include cost delta estimate computed by Optimize service; fall back to tiered estimate if telemetry delayed
Signal-gated progression should offer both system signals (SLOs) and custom eval checks (quality regression sets)
Limited the timeline compact view to 5 steps; show 'More' overflow that opens the expanded canvas to avoid cramped UI

notes_for_engineering: Backend will expose an optimistic snapshot create endpoint; design to show temporary 'creating snapshot' state
Cost delta service should expose an endpoint that accepts traffic percent for incremental computation; UI will debounce changes by 300ms
Signal-gated progression must accept a list of checks with comparator and threshold; design shows simplified label e.g., 'p95 < 300ms'
Implement instrumentation hooks for prototype simulation so Product can run A/B tests on adoption
